metric.definition: Order-to-delivery time for transformers, switchgear, generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators.

reading.body:
Critical equipment lead times now gate data center construction as hard as permits do, with transformers and switchgear stretching from months to years.

The pattern is a supply chain bottleneck in the electrical backbone of data centers. Transformers and switchgear connect a building to power, so their order-to-delivery time directly sets the earliest date new compute capacity can be energized. Generators, cooling plant, and high-end accelerators sit in the same queue, meaning even the most advanced hardware cannot escape the broader equipment schedule.

For AI, this matters because compute is downstream of buildings and power. A model run needs a finished data center, and a finished data center needs this equipment on site. When lead times stretch from months to years, they cap how fast AI capacity can scale regardless of accelerator supply or available capital.

What the data does not show is the actual number of months or years, how lead times differ by region or vendor, or whether they are still rising. It also covers only the five equipment categories listed and gives no price or volume data.
